author: f. g. mills
title: Claudia Tenney discusses tax policy, family business advocacy, and prison safety concerns
text:
Rep. Claudia Tenney, who represents New York’s 24th district in the U.S. Congress, recently posted a series of updates on her social media account addressing tax policy, family businesses, and public safety.
On March 10, 2026, Tenney shared statistics regarding tax refunds and recent federal tax changes: “Let’s look at the numbers so far. Average tax refund: $3,700+ 15M+ Americans claiming No Tax on Overtime 3.5M claiming No Tax on Tips The Trump Tax Cuts are putting money back where it belongs, in Americans’ pockets.”
The following day, March 11, Tenney highlighted her role as Co-Chair of the Congressional Family Business Caucus: “It’s a privilege to serve as Co-Chair of the bipartisan Congressional Family Business Caucus alongside @RepLouCorrea. Family-owned businesses support 83 million jobs and nearly 60% of the private workforce in the United States. As someone who helped run my family’s business, I”
Later that day, Tenney commented on a violent incident at Auburn Correctional Facility and criticized state leadership for inaction regarding correctional officer safety: “A corrections officer at Auburn was stabbed multiple times by a violent inmate. Four more officers were injured responding. One year after the corrections officers protested, Hochul and Albany Democrats have done nothing to fix these dangerous conditions. The HALT Act is”
Claudia Tenney has represented New York’s 24th district since 2021 after previously serving in the New York State Assembly from 2011 to 2016. Born in New Hartford in 1961 and currently residing in Canandaigua, she earned degrees from Colgate University and the University of Cincinnati.
